ARC: Iron Will (642)

=== EPISODE 21: Gumil (642)
## STEAM
Before Daeya — before the year that will stain his hands — the Sword of Silla rides alone to a small cavern lake in the hills: a bowl of black water under stone, cold enough to teach the bones manners. He has heard of the place the way a son hears of a hill his father once named a spring. His father came until the hill learned his walk. He comes the same way. Water. One question. The name.
The marshal’s robe falls at the rock lip before the steam has a name for him. Confucian blue on wet stone. He does not look up; looking up would be a request.
Steam lifts. They are already on the far rock: Narim with her ankles crossed like an elder sister who has seen this entrance before; Golhwa legs spread wide in the mist, chima hiked, as if the mist owed her heat; Hyullé a half-step behind them, knees pressed, eyes down on the water, not yet on him.
golhwa: You have his shoulders.
[FLASHBACK 595 The First Kim]
  Kim Seohyeon has been riding since dawn, the bright-blue robe stuck between his shoulders, and wants water more than a shrine. When heat breathes out of the hillside he names it a spring. Then he hears a laugh from no village he knows. He should turn the horse. He does not.
  Under the hill, three sisters have gone centuries without a man to look at. Golhwa keeps the heat in the stone, Hyullé the water, and Narim, the eldest, the moss and the roots and the rules. Golhwa has the warmest rock and is bored enough to bite it. Then the hill tells them about hooves on the road above.
  The news does not get Golhwa off the rock. She rides its warm ridge with her chima bunched at the hip, talking to it as if a man were already under her. Hyullé watches through the steam and pretends to be watching the steam. Narim calls it undignified and does not look away.
  narim: Golhwa. / The rock is not a man. Sit up.
  hyulle: We can be anything… / A fox. A crone. Let whoever comes take the water and go. I don’t want to want him already.
  hyulle: I haven’t even seen his stomach and my thighs are — sorry.
  narim: Then we try. Foxes first. If he laughs we change. / I pick the last face.
  For a breath they are foxes, three tails writing in the steam: one ember-red, one dripping, one with leaves caught in it. Golhwa likes it too much. Hyullé’s ears go flat. Narim shakes the fur off like a bad pin.
  golhwa: I look like a fox. I like it. / He would run. Fine. Old ladies.
  Then three crones at a well that is not a well, an ember in one sleeve, water at one hem, moss on one pair of shoulders. Golhwa hates the stoop. Hyullé almost stays; wanting is quieter in a crone’s face.
  narim: He’ll take the water and bless us and leave. / Younger, then. Not crones. The face a man stays for and calls mother.
  Then women old enough to have raised him, mouths kind and hungry at once. Narim almost keeps it; she has been an eldest that long.
  narim: He’ll want a mother. He’ll walk out of a mother. / Young. Sit so the silk sticks.
  hyulle: Young.
  They take the last shapes the way a hand takes a pin: white jeogori over olive, coral and pale blue. Three beautiful women on the far rock.
  He is still calling it a spring when the hill opens under his foot, and he comes up in a bowl of black water under stone.
  Wet through, he lets the robe fall, and the bright blue lies on the stone. He thinks he is alone, and walks into the steam.
  They have never seen a Kim. They look at his back first, then the jaw, the hands, the shoulders, and then, all three at once, back to the shoulders.
  Then their eyes go lower, past the wet chest to the dark water at his hips, which hides less than he thinks, and stay there. Golhwa’s mouth opens and does not close. Hyullé forgets to breathe. Narim hears herself swallow.
  Golhwa squints at him the way a painter squints at a wall, and talks to her sisters out of the side of her mouth.
  Put him in a panel. Chest. The water at his hips. I will look at that and nothing else.
  Don’t look. Looking makes the sound come out. A sound leaks out of her anyway.
  seohyeon: Who… / Who lives here. I was looking for water.
  narim: We do. You fell. / Sit— / Sit down before you fall in again.
  He looks at her as if she were kind, and Narim forgets what she was saying. A thousand years of practice, and she blames the steam.
  Sit down before I ask you to lay me on the rock, she does not say. She is the eldest.
  Golhwa steps in front of Hyullé like a door closing, Narim catches her wrist, and somehow Golhwa is already in the water up to her knees.
  golhwa: You already— wait. Hi. I’m Golhwa. That’s unnie. That’s Hyullé, she won’t say it unless you look at her first, which you should, but maybe don’t look at me like that or I am going to say the stupid thing.
  golhwa: Fuck— / Sorry. Hi.
  hyulle: I was going to. / Hello.
  seohyeon: Kim Seohyeon. / Are you… I mean. People.
  narim: Today. We are the mouths the hill uses when it is tired of being stone. / Not a village bath. I’m Narim.
  golhwa: Kim. / Say it again. No, I heard you. It just… sticks. Same sound as the steam. I like it.
  seohyeon: I should — the horse is up there.
  golhwa: I was going to say the ledge is warmer.
  golhwa: I was going to say I want you on it, between my legs.
  hyulle: The far ledge stays warm. / If you sit I can…
  hyulle: I’ll keep my knees together. That’s a lie. Somewhere warmer. On me.
  seohyeon: I have officers. I don’t need —
  The comedy goes out of the cave. Narim’s next words are not a woman’s. The hill answers.
  narim: Stand where you are. Do not climb the rock. Do not ask who we are. / One question. Spoken once, from the water. About what you will do — not what you want to hear. / The name is the offering. Kim.
  seohyeon: …Will the road take me home.
  narim: The road will take you home. The house will not stay there. / Keep the name in the palm they cannot see. A country will take your house and call the taking love.
  hyulle: The boy will need the name when they say he was never of them.
  golhwa: Leave before you ask a second. The second wears a crown. / …Sorry. That was the hill. This is me.
  seohyeon: I have a son. A few weeks. Yushin. / I don’t know what I would ask for him.
  They go still, and all three pairs of eyes go solid: green, cyan, ember.
  Seohyeon forgets he is naked. His son’s name is still in his mouth, and the hill has already spent it.
  The Hill: The child will be the measure two countries cannot share. / They will call him a blade and mean a border. / When they say he was never of them, the blade will still be Kim. / He will cut more than he is given. Don’t ask who bleeds.
  golhwa: That wasn’t a second. The hill was generous. This is me.
  Narim turns a river stone in her fingers, ordinary and grey and too warm for the cave, and puts it in his palm.
  narim: If it goes cold, you did not come as a petitioner. / If it stays warm, the hill will open. Same way. Water. One question. The name. Come back every time it is warm. Until you cannot climb. Then send the name.
  seohyeon: That is a lot to put on a boy who cannot sit up yet.
  golhwa: Come back though.
  narim: Then go.
  He climbs out wearing nothing but water and the stone, and nobody on the far rock has the manners to look away.
  golhwa: He looked at me first.
  hyulle: …He looked at the water.
  golhwa: …Which is worse. / Next time he’s mine. Not yours.
  hyulle: If he does… I want the face next time. / I’ll hide. I’ll look anyway.
  Hyullé’s footprint takes a long time to fade from the rock he did not sit on. Golhwa’s foot swings. Narim’s smile is small, and tired.
  He rides home with three names and a stone that will not cool, and tells the next post it was a spring. Then he keeps coming back, more eagerly than any son will, until the hill learns his walk.
  Years later he is grey at the temples, and the counsel has not changed: one question from the water, one name. When it is done he does not reach for the robe, and this time he sits on the warm ledge.
  seohyeon: You three are going to kill an old man. / I came back anyway. The horse knows the way better than I do.
  golhwa: Grey already, First Kim?
  narim: The hill remembers a younger walk. / Tonight we will see what is left.
  hyulle: …Hm.
  Golhwa does not stay on her rock. She reaches him first and kisses him like a woman who has waited decades for it, and he kisses her back as if he had waited just as long.
  She settles into his lap on the warm ledge with her coral silk bunched at the hip and takes him in slowly, then not slowly at all, and the quiet of the spring does not survive it. She came to mock an old man. His arms are still iron under the wet skin, and he sets the pace without asking.
  When it breaks over her she is loud about it, and he follows a breath later, holding her so she does not fall wrong. Afterwards she lies against his wet shoulder, trembling, hair everywhere, until the cry turns into breath and the breath into a ruined laugh.
  Grey at the temples and he is still under me. I screamed. He stayed. Kiss. Inside. Ride. He filled me. Mine.
  Jealousy turns into sharing the way steam turns into weather, all at once and wet. The sisters leave their rock. Narim means to sit like an eldest and lasts one breath. Hyullé climbs into his lap last, without a word, and when her silence breaks it breaks against his chest.
  Dawn finds the four of them asleep on the warm ledge, tangled in wet silk: Golhwa still where she won first, her throat raw, Narim with her mouth almost on his lined cheek, Hyullé curled against his side.
  In the morning he leaves before the road remembers him. The stone stays warm until the year he can no longer climb, and then, as he was told, he sends the name.
Now the name stands waist-deep in the same black water, scrubbing the road off his forearms.
Golhwa’s legs stay spread wide on the wet rock, chima hiked. She is wet enough to take him from here. A thread of it finds her lip and she does not wipe it. His father’s shoulders. Worse. Hyullé’s knees stay pressed, eyes down, silk soaked through between them, and she answers nothing because if she opens her mouth it will be a sound. Narim’s silk clings and her next breath is late. Kim. Ours. Fuck him. The marshal looks once and the spring does not hide much — he is rock-hard in the black bowl and pretends the water is a wall. His father would have teased. He quotes the queen.
narim: Kim Yushin. You wash like a man who thinks dirt is the only thing that sticks. / It isn’t. The water’s on your stomach and I haven’t looked away.
golhwa: Leave the sermon, unnie. He’s naked. We can be honest. / Come closer, Yushin— I want that on my tongue before she makes it a lesson.
She has been on that rock since his father left, moaning at nobody, picturing him under her. She wants him to grab her and fuck her into the stone. If he stays put she will come across. The most popular man in Silla, and he came back to their water. Hyullé’s eyes go to the waterline and stay. Narim forgets the sermon for one breath.
She goes in like a tiger. Wink. Knees open. Steam that looks like it is coming off her skin.
golhwa: Don’t stand there like that. I can see all of you and you’re just letting me. / I will come across. Open your knees. I’m not swimming over to talk.
hyulle: …Golhwa. / He came to rest.
hyulle: I still want my mouth on him. I’m sorry. I’m not.
yushin: …Who are you three. / If this is a dream, make it shorter. I have a border to cut.
The comedy goes out of the cave again. He asked who they are. That is not a question they answer.
narim: That is not a question we answer. Stand where you are. One question. What you will do. / You came as your father came. The flirting is free. The hill is not. / Take Baekje’s forts if you must. Do not take Baekje’s hurry. / And stop standing there wet, like you don’t know what that does to the three of us.
hyulle: And… if a man from the north offers you a door… / …look who holds the latch on the other side. / Sorry. I — I was staring at your chest. The latch too. I meant both.
golhwa: She meant it. Don’t apologise for being right, Hyullé. / Also — your friend with the pink name. Chunchu. / He will kneel in rooms you would burn. That is not weakness. It cuts later.
golhwa: You, though. If you’re going to kneel, kneel here, where I can feel it.
yushin: I hear you. / But Her Majesty —
golhwa: Ugh… / “Her Majesty.” “Her Majesty.” / What does that mortal have that we don’t? A chair.
golhwa: I’ve got my legs open and you’re still saying her name.
golhwa: Stay with us, Yushin~~
golhwa: Stay— in my lap. Don’t make me beg when my legs are already open.
She wants him in her, not bowing. The title can keep the forts. Unnie can keep the sermon.
narim: Golhwa. / When they ask if a woman can hold the west, do not answer for her. Take the forts on her count. Slow. She will look like she planned it. / And when the count is done, come back dripping. I am not finished with you.
hyulle: …The binyeo is pretty. The face is tired. / …He can go.
hyulle: I only — wanted my thighs around him before the road. Warm was the polite word.
yushin: Forts. Slow. Her count. I have it. / Dedication is not a flirtation you three get to bill me for. / …But the water helps. Already.
golhwa: Hear that? He thanked the water. Not us. / Fine. Go play marshal. Next time, leave the armour — and that mortal — outside the cave.
golhwa: Leave the hard part in here.
narim: Golhwa. Hyullé. / The warm ledge around the bend — and the herbs in the cleft. Both of you. / Go on. The marshal still has ears for counsel… and I still have a mouth for it.
narim: I’m going to use the mouth.
golhwa: Herbs? For a bath? / …Unnie. If you’re about to sermon him alone, I’m billing you for boredom. If you’re about to sit on him, I’m billing you for theft.
hyulle: …Yes, unnie. / We’ll — we’ll be quick.
hyulle: Don’t you dare finish him before I hear it.
They go. Mist takes the younger two the way water takes a thrown stone — a bright disturbance, then nothing. Yushin is alone with Narim, and for the first time he understands that being alone with any of them is not the same as being safe.
narim: You thanked the water. / I am not water. / Come here, Kim Yushin
narim: — I want you in my mouth before the border teaches you how to refuse.
yushin: Narim— / You just told them we are steam.
narim: I told them. / The counsel was real. So is this. / Stay. Not for the queen. Not for the road.
narim: For the part of you that’s hard, pretending the steam has no mouth.
She crosses the black water as if it owes her a path. Close enough that the steam becomes her breath on his mouth. Her palm finds the wet line of his collarbone — not Golhwa’s tease, not Hyullé’s apology — a quiet claim, and when she kisses him there is laughter under it, and hunger, and the patience of someone who has been watching him undress for longer than this visit.
yushin: …This is not counsel. / And I — I still have to leave.
narim: Of course you do. / Mainland boys always do. / So kiss me like someone who will be late for the border
narim: — and put your hand under the silk while you still can.
He does. Or she makes him. Hard to tell, in water that warm. Her mouth opens under his; her thigh finds his hip against the rock; for a few breaths the marshal of Silla is only a guest who has drifted too far from shore — and likes it, disastrously.
narim: There. / Deeper. The steam won’t tell. / …Unless my sisters do. Don’t you dare be gentle.
golhwa: The herbs were already— unnie, his mouth is on you. I can see it. Move.
Mist tears. Golhwa first, arms full of nothing useful; Hyullé a half-step behind, eyes huge. Narim’s hand is still on him. Nobody moves for one long, ridiculous second — then the cavern remembers how to be loud.
golhwa: UNNIE. / You sent us for herbs so you could—?! / What does that mortal have that we don’t — wait. What do you have that we don’t?!
golhwa: Him. In you. Get off, or share.
hyulle: …Unnie. / You said we were his steam. / Steam doesn’t… hold like that.
hyulle: I was going to. I kept my knees together so I wouldn’t, and you sat down first.
narim: Put the herbs down. / And close your mouths before the marshal remembers he can still dress. / …Hyullé. The ledge. Warm it anyway — he will run, and he will pretend this was weather.
narim: You can still taste where I was.
yushin: …I should go. / The Queen will need me before the year turns.
golhwa: Oh now he thanks the exit. / Fine. Next time nobody leaves the rock. I mean it.
golhwa: I’ll sit on his face until the queen’s numbers fall out.
golhwa: Stay with us, Yushin~~
golhwa: — or at least stop letting unnie eat first.
hyulle: …The ledge is still warm. / If you want. Before the road. / I won’t — look. Much.
hyulle: I’ll look lower.
hyulle: I’m sorry. Come here anyway.
He dresses in the cold with three pairs of eyes on him and one mouth still tasting of forest. When he looks again they are back on the far rock — as if nothing happened — except Golhwa’s foot swings harder, and Hyullé’s footprint takes longer to fade, and Narim’s smile is the smallest, most dangerous thing in the cave. He rides south with counsel under his ribs… and an invitation he can no longer pretend not to have answered.
## BOTH ROADS
They ask him to choose. Gaya blood or Silla marshal. Fortress count or cavern counsel. The yard’s perfection or the one room that does not ask him for a victory.
He refuses the fork they keep drawing for him. Gaya blood or Silla marshal. Fortress count or cavern counsel. He rides from the cliff-fortress with the horse still smelling of the border, shaves at the cave mouth because the sisters keep that rule, and sits where the dark water meets the bright valley — three faint spirits at his back, a kingdom that still doubts his loyalty ahead.
narim: You do not have to pick a country to wash in. / Wash. Then go be useful to whichever one still needs you. If you get hard on the road, that was my mouth. Don’t thank the water for it.
yushin: …Both need me. / That is the trouble.
## THE MARSHAL’S STEAM
Yushin does not bring everyone to the lake. He brings Chunchu — once — because a man who will invent rooms the Council never votes on should learn what steam does to cleverness.
At the mouth he borrows a razor and makes a mess of dignity. Magenta silk leaves his shoulders. He walks in with nothing on but water. He still thinks a lake cannot surprise a man who invents rooms.
They smell the name before they finish his face. Steam off Golhwa’s skin; her legs stay spread. Water down Hyullé’s chin; her knees stay pressed, eyes down. A leaf that will not fall beside Narim. He keeps the black bowl as a wall. The spring does not hide much — letter or sword, he is already standing in the water the way every Kim does when he looks at them. They do not ask his rank.
golhwa: Oh — a soft one. / Yushin, you brought us a letter instead of a sword. Hi. I’m Golhwa. Don’t look at me like that or I’ll say what I want to do with the soft one.
golhwa: Come closer— I want to feel if the letter made you shy or hard.
She has been on the rock picturing a letter-soft mouth. Soft ones last. She cannot sit. She wants him to pin her until she goes insane.
chunchu: I am inventing a kingdom. / …Preferably with fewer surprises in the water.
narim: Sit— / Sit down before you invent it standing. I’m Narim. We are the mouths the hill uses. Wisdom, if you ask once, from the water. The marshal already knows the door. I would like to know your mouth.
He looks at her like she is a clerk who can be managed. Narim cannot finish the first Sit. Out of breath. Sit down before I ask you to put that clever mouth on me, she does not say. Fuck. She is the eldest. Hyullé says nothing. In her head he is already on her. She looks like she will explode.
hyulle: Hello. I’m already wet. Don’t make me say why.
chunchu: Will a room the Council never votes on hold. / That is the only question I have that is not a joke.
The comedy goes out of the cave. All three pairs of eyes go solid — green, cyan, ember. One voice. Three mouths.
THE HILL: Build the room. Do not put your name on the door. / A country will take a house and call the taking love. You already know that sentence. Use it.
golhwa: That was the hill. This is me. / Come closer anyway. Soft ones last. I can’t sit. My legs won’t close while you’re looking.
He leaves with nothing on but water until the mouth. The magenta is still on the stone. He looks at the path as if it were a map he intends to redraw. One sister watches him go. Another cannot speak. He never asks to return. He never entirely forgets the steam.
## DAEYA FORTRESS
King Euija (42) reads Silla’s border the way he reads everything — patiently, and only once. Daeya is young at the top and hollow underneath. He sends the General Yunchung with ten thousand men, and in Surabol nobody’s dreams change, because the people who should be dreaming badly are at a wedding’s afterglow.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Seondeok, yr. 11 (642), 8th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 118] The Baekje general Yunchung led troops, attacked, and took Daeya Fortress. The dodok Ichan Pumsuk, and the saji Jukjuk and Yongseok, died there.
Pumsuk (24) is the head general of Daeya, despite his young age, because he is a Noble.
gumil: Putting a boy this green in charge of the border — does that make any sense?
gumil: Ah, forgotten what country this is? To them we’re not even dirt~ / Say “True Bone” and the heavens part on their own~~
gumil: Why was I even born in this wretched country, to suffer like this!!
Maehwa is the poorest woman in Daeya and the one every eye in it finds first. She is thirty-one. She stopped pretending not to know what happens to a room when she walks into it a long time ago, and the fortress has never forgiven her for it.
gumilwife: The men in this fortress. They all smell the same. / Dirt, drink… and looking when they think I won’t notice.
gumil: Cover yourself when you go out.
gumilwife: Buy me clothes, then. / Everything I own refuses to fit.
gumil: …You know what I am paid.
gumilwife: I do. / Which is why everyone looks.
By noon the packed-earth yard splits. Porters, smiths, the boys who haul grain cluster at the well-post as if the work had always been there. Maehwa crosses alone — teal-sage silk, one red sash, celebrity distance. They do not come closer. She does not invite them.
🗣: Look at that hem… / No — the waist. The waist. / That's Gumil's wife. / I know. That's why it's worse—
She hears every unfinished sentence. Bored chin, and the men keep looking anyway — dirt under the nails, the same sour drink on the breath. Lower class, all of them, and she is tired of being their festival. Tired, and still walking as if the yard were built around her.
gumilwife: That is a road. / Do not stand in it.
One of them forgets to close his mouth. She turns just enough. The hem stays a breath too long — teal silk telling on the hip, the wooden sprig pin catching the light — and she lets him have that second like a coin she can afford to drop. Then the silk falls back. She will not let him close.
🗣: Just now— / I saw. I saw. / …She didn't even say anything.
She leaves them wrecked on the packed earth and almost smiles — a small, private thing, gone before the well-post. The yard is about the curve she takes with her.
## INSIDE THE FORTRESS
Before the True Bone’s horse is even a rumour, the inside of Daeya already has a weather, and the weather is her. The well-post learns her hip first. Packed earth. Timber eaves. Men turn their heads as she passes. The wives they brought watch her instead of the water.
🗣: That chest— no, the waist. / Both. It’s both. / That’s Gumil’s wife. Why is she built like—
She does not look at them. She places a hand on the red sash as if it had slipped, and it has not slipped. The storehouse door is a dark mouth. Yellow sleeves in the shadow forget they have wives standing next to them. The wives do not forget. Thirty-one. The silk is poor. The body is not.
🗣: Watch the hand. That’s on purpose. / Don’t look at her. / I can’t. That’s the problem.
On the inner stair she lets the jeogori fall another finger. The post takes the silhouette. Men turn on the steps. Wives on the landing go still. They will tell themselves they were looking at the stair. They were looking at the curve under the ochre.
The night before the True Bone arrives, the room is only a lamp and the two of them. Maehwa’s teal silk opens at the shoulder. Gumil’s yellow sleeve comes off as if the month’s pay had never been the argument. They still know how to find each other. They will not know how tomorrow.
gumilwife: Tomorrow the boy arrives. / Today… only today. / Keep your hand on my waist. / It does not have to be a True Bone hand.
gumil: I know. / I know. / …Leave tomorrow for tomorrow.
They stop talking. The lamp is too small for manners. The red sash comes off the way it always does in this room — one impatient pull — and the teal silk follows it onto the boards. His yellow sleeve is already gone. Thirty-one, and she still puts him where she wants him: on his back, her hand around him, then sitting until he is in to the hilt, the way winter has always started in this house.
gumilwife: Tomorrow can wait. / Tonight you stay under me. / Don’t use a name. / Just… stay.
She knows his body the way a person knows a door they have opened every winter. When he nuts it is with her name, not a rank — a familiar load, nothing stupid-young about it, and she keeps him in until it is finished and then a little after, rolling her hips so none of it goes to waste. They sleep facing the same wall. In the morning the silk will go back on as if the night had been ordinary. It never is.
Then a True Bone takes the fortress — twenty-four, clean hands, and a wife whose father is the most important man in Silla.
chunchu: Th-the father of that child… Lady Munhee’s… I mean… / It’s me!
At the feast the wine finds Pumsuk first. Clean ice-blue silk. Crescent band. A cup he is not tasting. Then the lamp-line is hers — Maehwa walking the cheap hanging lamps like she built them, dirtied green jeogori, ochre chima washed too many times, the red sash tied by habit. Poor cloth against a dark hall. His clothes stay clean. Hers do not.
He talks to the cup. It does not help. The training is a joke tonight. Heart-pupils. A thread of drool he will not wipe. She is only a green shape in the lamp behind him, and that is enough.
The feast is not a private room. It is every man in Daeya and the families they brought. She walks the aisle. Bowls stop. Necks turn. The wives watch her, not the food, and the watching is already a fight. He looks at her instead of his own table. The families are still eating. She is already working.
She does it in public the way she does it in a dark room. A plum from a tray. A hand on her own hip, then on the sash, then — as if by accident — at the inner thigh where the ochre splits when she sits. She has practised this. The boy in ice-blue counts without meaning to. Twenty-four. The training does not cover a woman who knows where to put her hands.
gumilwife: The plum— ah, it’s the mouth, not the cup. / The hand? Here. I meant that. / Twenty-four and you can see all of it.
I should look at my own table. I am looking at her chest. At the split of the chima. At the place a general is not supposed to name. I like women built like that. I have always liked it. I am going to hate myself in a bed that is not hers.
He does the correct thing. He stands. He bows to a feast that has not asked him to leave. He goes to sleep like a man with a pink room waiting. The pallet does not take him.
One dying lamp. One cold pallet. One feast still lit down the hall. How long can a True Bone lie still…?

=== EPISODE 22: Maehwa (642)
A man is measured by his self-control.
## HE TRIES TO SLEEP
Ice-blue on dark timber. One dying lamp. Eyes open. The hall comes with him anyway — her hip, her mouth, the plum, the hand that was not an accident. He tries to sleep and the hall comes with him. A True Bone should be able to close his eyes. He is twenty-four and hard in the dark and he knows exactly why.
This fire. I did not light it. She walked the lamps and it caught. I have a wife. I have a name. I have a cock that will not listen. The curve of her — I like that. I have always liked that. === EPISODE 24: Yeon’s Massacre (642)
Yeon's father dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The seal should pass to the son. The Summit takes the whole summer to admit it. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet. The king is in attendance.

October cold sits under the eaves. The lamps are already lit when the Five Commanderies take their seats — wine first, then meat, then the old joke that Pyongyang never runs out of either. Each commander wears a ring-pommel sword at his hip, the three-legged crow stamped in the ring. The hall smells of sesame oil and autumn horse-sweat brought in on Eastern boots.

southcmd: Yeon…! / Samhan… the Samhan His Majesty named—
gesomun: Son Daeha. / You asked for men, not speeches. / I am taking the men.
He draws the Southern ring-pommel from a belt that no longer needs it. One crow. One weight on the spine to come.
Then the Northern Commander. He would not freeze another winter while the capital counted his remounts twice.
northcmd: The horses… still in… the warehouses…
gesomun: Go Ul. / …The three villages. I remember them.
The Northern crow joins the first. Outside, a horse screams in the yard and then does not.
The Western Commander had warned that this would gift the Tang a road. He dies looking west, as if the road might still be argued shut.
westcmd: The Liao… / The Emperor’s drums…
gesomun: You were right about the road.
Three crows. The hall’s lamps lean as if listening.
Lee Gaesa is not a commandery banner, but he was the Summit’s mouth the day the word traitor was first set on Yeon’s name. Tonight the mouth has wine in it, and then nothing.
leegaesa: Traitor…! / That day… I…
gesomun: Lee Gaesa. / You gave me the word. / I am keeping it.
Four. The word he was given becomes metal he can wear.
Last of the banners: his uncle. The soft voice that told a nephew to sit down, because the Summit does not run on prophecies.
gusesa: Nephew… / A feast… like this…
gesomun: Uncle. / You told me to sit down. / …. / A Yeon takes this one from a Yeon.
Five ring-pommels. Five crows. Yeon wipes none of them clean.
He finally approaches King Youngryu for the final blow. The crown has slid. The Samhan dream is still in the king’s mouth, too late to be a budget.
yeongnyu: Gesomun… / With gold… decades… / The King for All…
gesomun: Your Majesty. / The gold was never going to be enough. He had already priced your head. / May You live ten thousand years.
Yeon places each of the Five Blades onto his own back.
He steps into the doorway with the blades on his back. Red-wing chalgap fills the door.
gesomun: Loyal men of Goguryeo — hear the words of Yeon Gesomun! / In the south, Baekje and Silla covet us, / and in the west the Second Emperor comes this way, butchering nation after nation! / And all the while an incompetent king and rotten ministers shut their eyes to the world and lead this country down the road to ruin!! / Silla and the East, then Baekje the next day, then the Tang!
gesomun: But what of the people? We have nowhere else to go! / We live on this land, we die on it, and we are the ones who bleed every time they come! / The world will call us mad! Of course — to take your own fate in your own hands has always looked like madness to the world!
gesomun: No one is coming to save us!! Only we can do it — with our own hands!!
In the aftermath, Yeon enthrones the king’s nephew as King Bojang and creates a new position for himself, as the Supreme Commander.
[diagram high-summit]
He makes one more appointment before the blood is dry. Dosuryu — an old friend of the Yeon house, one of the few men who has ever told him no and lived — is named Grand Herald, a post that did not exist until the banquet needed a voice that was not the throne’s.
dosuryu: Grand Herald… / I have had you by the scruff since your father was alive. / And now you want that mouth to read the country aloud?
gesomun: If you will not, who will. / That Bojang… I only need the name. / The one who speaks to the 겨레 is you.
dosuryu: Very well. / Only — for as long as you still listen to me. / If you stop, I am a herald, not a friend.
Yeon listens. Not always. Often enough that the court learns which door to fear besides his.
gesomun: You there… what is your name?
bojang: M-my name? My surname is Go—
gesomun: You there… what is your name?
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun · bk. 21, Goguryeo Annals — King Yeongnyu, yr. 25 (642), 10th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 312 · cf. Zizhi Tongjian Tang Zhenguan 16] When the guests arrived he killed them all, some hundred men; he galloped into the palace and murdered the king, set up the king’s brother’s son Jang as sovereign, made himself Mangniji, and monopolized the state.
After the blood dries Yeon does something the temples will not forgive and the chronicles barely record: he sends for Tang masters of the Way. The point is to starve the Buddhist monk aristocracy of the prestige they wear like armour. Incense changes. Halls cool. One young monk named Shinsung learns how to wait.
gesomun: Pray quieter. / Or pray to something that does not own half the capital.
shinsung: Amitabha.
## AFTER THE KNIVES
In the markets the news arrives the way all bad news arrives — ahead of the official word, behind the smell of smoke. Grain sellers count on their fingers. Children stop racing. Someone says banquet and means blood.
Vendor: The king… they say he’s dead. / The commanders too. More than a hundred. And the Red Sun of Pyongyang — they say he strapped their blades to his back.
Wall sentry: Some say the Eternal General saved us. / The court was sharpening first. We were next. Commoners… we say that name before we say Yeon.
goguard_a: Those blades… they say he strapped five of them to his back. / The commanders’ swords. On his own spine.
goguard_b: By Haemosu’s light… incredible… / No — terrifying. Incredible, and terrifying.
Quiet man: Still… is butchering a banquet the same as saving a country.
Wall sentry: Don’t say that on the wall.
On the barracks steps the same argument runs until the drum tells them to stop arguing and start marching.
The capital learns a new etiquette. Remaining officials swear loyalty not to the nephew-king’s smile but to the Supreme Commander’s door. Men who hesitate are removed before winter — titles stripped, names scratched from the rolls, a few bodies found where the river turns. The foreign hostels lock from the outside. Tribute missions that once bought another quiet decade are cancelled mid-packing; silk meant for Chang’an stays in the warehouses.
March boots outrank court shoes. Drums outrank flutes. Monks keep their heads down while the new Taoist masters walk the halls Yeon starved of incense. Envoys who still ask for audience are told the kingdom is closed for inventory — of grain, of blades, of who belongs inside the walls. Goguryeo under Yeon watches the roads in and trusts almost none of them.
At night the house is quieter than the city. Yeon’s wife has kept three boys from the sound of cheering that is not quite cheer. She waits until the lamps are few enough that even a Supreme Commander looks like a husband.
yeonwife: What will Tang say… / Silla too. Baekje. / Massacre. Traitor. / How those outside will name our people… even thinking of it—
gesomun: Listen… it doesn’t matter what they’ll say about us. / Do you hear me? It doesn’t matter at all — zero. Not even one bit.
gesomun: Did their ancestors die for this dirt? / Will they be standing here when it is our turn to bleed?
gesomun: So whatever they say out there about our people, our way of living — / not one second of your life. Please. / Look at me. Promise me.
yeonwife: …I promise. / Only — when the boys are grown, tell them that too.
He nods. Outside, the drums keep time for a kingdom learning to live with its doors shut.
A kingdom with its doors shut, and a man with five swords on his back. Naturally, Chunchu wants to go and knock…!

=== EPISODE 25: Chunchu & Yeon (642)
Since Daeya fell, Chunchu has had one request for the Queen: send him north to Pyongyang, to beg Goguryeo for troops against Baekje. She has not said yes.
The news reaches Surabol about a month late, the way news from the north usually does.
sunduk: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
yushin: Well I never… I thought our country would fall first, and Goryeo goes ahead of us. So who is this subject?
alchun: They call him the Eternal General — Yeon, or Gesomun. Commoners say Red Sun of Pyongyang when they think courts cannot hear.
chunchu: “Yeon Gesomun”…
Chunchu asks again, and this time the Queen lets him go. Nobody offers to go instead.
yushin: If you go and do not return, Hangyul’s hooves will trample Goryeo underfoot without fail.
chunchu: I will return within sixty days. If I have not returned by then, there will be no promise of meeting again.
He leaves by the west gate of Wolseong on Hadong, a lean red bay he named for summer and winter, because a diplomat’s horse, he says, has to stand in both. Yushin walks beside the bridle as far as the gate and no farther, which for Yushin is a speech.
yushin: Sixty days. / He knows the way back. Even if you forget.
chunchu: You’re saying he’s smarter than me. / …Hear that, Hadong? Yushin trusts you.
yushin: It’s you I don’t trust.
Pyongyang lets him in through the red gate and keeps him waiting on the stair. When someone finally comes down, it is Dosuryu, the Grand Herald.
chunchu: Your Excellency…
Chunchu requests to see the king.
King Bojang makes his request — though the word his is doing generous work, and everyone in the room knows for whom.
gesomun: Oi, Silla — why the long face?
gesomun: And call it Goguryeo. / Not Goryeo. I am not tired enough to shorten my own country.
chunchu: Goguryeo, then — if the chronicles insist. / Most men I meet have already shortened it.
chunchu: You would take this land’s crisis as your chance, and demand territory? / As a subject I have no say, so I await your judgement. And now — I take my leave…
gesomun: You come into another man’s house, refuse his price, and still look me in the eye. / Has Silla no pride left? Or is it only you?
chunchu: I know no such thing as pride. / Pride is a decoration for men who can afford to lose. / I know where I am going. There is nothing in this room large enough to stand in the way.
gesomun: …
Outside the door, two Goguryeo soldiers have been listening the way soldiers listen — professionally, and for sport.
goguard_a: Did you hear him? / …Said it to the Mangniji’s face. Didn’t blink once.
goguard_b: Silla men talk like that when they want to walk into Yumla’s court stylishly.
goguard_a: Bet you a dried fish he crawls out on his knees.
goguard_b: Bet you two he cries.
The door opens. Chunchu is escorted out between two attendants. His left hand is a red glove. Blood runs off the wrist and dots the stone like a trail someone meant to follow.
goguard_b: …Ah?
goguard_a: Ah——??
goguard_b: Why is there blood. By the Holy King’s bow, why is there so much blood.
goguard_a: Did—— did the Mangniji cut him?
dosuryu: Move. Prison.
goguard_b: Prison? The man brushed past the death escort and he still has that face on.
They put him in a cell with a window. That is meant to be a courtesy. The courtesy does not include a physician.
chunchu: (…Good. He looked. He will remember looking.)
What the guards do not know — what nobody in the corridor knows — is whose blade opened the hand. That answer waits in another man’s memory, for another meeting.
Chunchu has no physician, but he has a sleeve, and sewn into it is what a Silla envoy carries when he expects to be robbed. Somehow it reaches Seon Dohae, the king’s favourite, without passing through any door the Mangniji is watching.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Chunchu in Goguryeo, 642)] Chunchu secretly gave three hundred measures of blue cloth to the king’s favourite, Seon Dohae.
Seon Dohae arrives with a jar of wine and no guards, which is either courage or an arrangement. He pours two cups, drinks both when Chunchu does not reach for his, and starts talking about the sea.
seondohae: Can’t hold a cup with a hand like that. I’ll drink it for you. / …Tell me, my lord. Ever heard the one about the turtle and the rabbit?
chunchu: …Even if I had, I’d like to hear it from you.
seondohae: The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea had a daughter with a sick heart. The physician said a rabbit’s liver would cure her. / No rabbits in the sea. So the turtle climbs up on land and strikes up a conversation with a rabbit. / “Out in the middle of the sea there’s an island. Clear water, fruit everywhere, no hawks, no eagles. Come on. Get on my back.”
chunchu: And the rabbit got on.
seondohae: Got right on. The Holy King ran across a river on turtles’ backs, so turtles are generally trustworthy. Generally. / Two or three li out, the turtle turns his head and confesses. Actually, we need your liver. / And do you know what the rabbit said?
chunchu: …
seondohae: “Oh dear. I’m descended from spirits, I can take out my insides and wash them. My chest’s been tight lately, so I left my liver drying under a rock. Let’s go back and fetch it.” / The turtle believed him and turned around. The moment they touched the shore, the rabbit was into the grass. / “Idiot. Who lives without a liver?”
Seon Dohae refills his own cup and looks at nothing in particular. Chunchu looks at his ruined hand for a long time, then laughs once, quietly, the way a man laughs when a lock he has been picking turns over.
chunchu: …Could I trouble you for paper? / The left one’s in no state, so I’ll use the right.
The letter goes to the king, not the Mangniji. The passes were Goguryeo's to begin with, it says, and once Chunchu is home he will ask his sovereign to give them back. He signs with a flourish. He has no intention of doing any such thing. His drinking partner, finishing the jar, has no intention of mentioning it.
On the sixtieth day Yushin starts counting out men. He does not ask the Queen first.
However, when the Eternal General hears of the Sword of Silla, he lets the most cunning man in Samhan go immediately.
chunchu: Huh?
chunchu: Yushin is coming!
yushin: I don’t quite know either… perhaps he lost his nerve when he heard you were coming!
chunchu: (The Eternal General… a more fearsome man than I expected…)
On the Silla side of the border, in a camp that should not exist, Yushin has brought the horse. Hadong is tied at the front of the lines with an empty saddle, the way some armies carry an empty chair. When Chunchu comes down the last hill on foot, thinner, the left hand bound against his chest, the horse sees him before the men do.
chunchu: …Hadong. / You got fat. Yushin fed you better than they fed me.
yushin: Hand. / …Give it here. The right one.
Chunchu cannot close the left hand on a rein, so Yushin ties both reins around his right wrist himself, in a knot he learned in the drill yard for men who have been shot. He says nothing about the hand, and Chunchu says nothing about the camp.
gesomun: …What? The Sword of the Divine Country is coming? / …Let him go.
dosuryu: Sir?
gesomun: Did you not hear me? Release Chunchu. / But truly… who is this Chunchu — the most cunning man in Samhan — that the Sword of Silla comes for him himself?
dosuryu: Who is this Sword of Silla, that the Eternal General behaves so? / Surely… you are not afraid?
gesomun: Boy — even a man ready to die does not poke a tiger for no reason. / The day will come when we face Yushin… / but not over something like Chunchu.
One envoy left Pyongyang bleeding. Whose blade was it? Now the King of Baekje walks in on purpose, laughing…!

=== EPISODE 26: Euija & Yeon (642)
News of Yeon’s Massacre reaches Baekje.
euija: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
euija: This is an opportunity…
He asks for troops. He asks twice.
gesomun: Have you come to see the king?
euija: No… I have come to see the one with real power.
gesomun: He does not grant an audience to just anyone.
euija: Tell him who I am, and he will come at once.
Yeon is surprised that the new King of Baekje has come personally.
euija: I hear you ploughed under the king and the whole noble faction? That one thing, I rather envy…
gesomun: Could you not do the same on your side?
euija: Look here — I am the king myself. / General Gesomun— / I would be called a tyrant and killed the next day, ah.
gesomun: Your people killed a king of ours on that wall out there. You can see it from this room.
euija: And Hansung? You put our king’s head on your own wall and called it a season’s work.
[FLASHBACK 475 Hansung]
  Once, a Goguryeo king came south and took Baekje’s old capital. The Baekje king tried to run. They caught him and killed him at the foot of a mountain. Baekje has not forgotten. Goguryeo has not apologised.
euija: Besides… of the two men in this room, only one has actually murdered a king of Goryeo. It was not me.
Yeon puts the blade on the table between them. Not pointed at anything. Just there.
gesomun: Give me one reason I should not cut you down with this blade where you stand…!
euija: Pfft—hahahahahaha!!
euija: Gesomun… you may know how to command an army, but in politics you are plainly a novice. Do you know what politics is? / Politics is alchemy. The alchemy of manufacturing a justification for what I already want to do. / Do you know how many people in the surrounding countries admire you right now? / Yeon Gesomun — the man who ploughed under the corrupt officials and will bring a new age. / But… kill the King of Baekje now, and word reaches every one of those countries. / You become a madman who enjoys killing kings. Nothing else.
gesomun: This land is not just dirt. / Goguryeo is the land of the holy king, descended from the sun god. / The Holy King. Son of Haemosu. A line that came down from heaven.
euija: Pfft—!! / Hahahahaha!! / Wait… wait. The Supreme Commander of a country — / a grown man, a man who leads a kingdom — / still believes in spirits and sun chariots?
gesomun: Do not laugh. / He came down from heaven. He opened a kingdom with a bow. / That blood — is the bone of this 겨레.
euija: Oh, certainly. There was probably a man who shot well. / The rest is a story for keeping people in line. / To make a farmer kneel, a sun god is cheaper than a sword.
gesomun: …So that is what your palace teaches. / I grew up in the marches. What the marches tell — is not a lie.
Neither man yields. The room keeps both versions: a bowman who founded a country — and a heaven that may or may not have sent him.
Yeon asks for the same thing he asked Chunchu for. He has only ever had one price.
gesomun: The land north of the pass was Goguryeo’s. Return it, and I will send relief troops.
dosuryu: What nerve, to come before him like that…!
euija: Listen — I am the king of a country. A king is not a man. / I made my arrangements even for death, and gave warning abroad beforehand. / Kill me and all you get is a newer, angrier King of Baekje on the throne.
gesomun: Not a man, you say…
euija: They have a saying in Silla — that slaves are not counted as people. / Funny, is it not? The bottom is not a person, and the top is not a person either. / Everyone who gets to be a person is wedged in between.
euija: Look at this map. / Silla has no trade route at all — for Tang, for Tianzhu, for the western regions, there is only this one harbour. / Danghangseong would be the right target.
euija: We have our own mouth — the White River under Sabi. / Clan berths stacked like teeth. Cut Danghangseong and Silla starves for partners; keep our river and we eat either way.
gesomun: You sound like a harbour clerk. / Good. Kings who forget docks start wars they cannot feed.
gesomun: Do you know a “Kim Chunchu” of Silla?
euija: Kim Chunchu? First I have heard of him… royalty? Why?
gesomun: Just… curious. He does not seem to care for you much. / He spoke of being rid of you, hands folded in prayer.
euija: Chunchu… whoever he is, a man who stores things up like that is no easy sort. / But I do not fear a man who kneels to others.
For a moment Yeon’s eyes go somewhere else — to a door, to a hand, to a stare that did not ask to be liked.
[FLASHBACK 642 the hand]
  After the territory talk the room had gone quiet in the wrong way. Yeon had asked if the man had no pride. The answer had been worse than no.
  chunchu: I know no such thing as pride. / I know only my goal.
  Then Chunchu had reached to his own belt, drawn a short blade, and driven it through his own left hand — clean, deliberate, eyes never leaving Yeon’s face — and held the wound up like a seal.
  chunchu: This is how much of myself I will spend. / Do not ask me for pride. Ask me what I am willing to ruin.
  gesomun: ……
  Yeon remembers the stare more than the blood. Hot, dry, almost joyful. The stare of a man who had decided the room would believe him, and had paid in advance.
gesomun: That Chunchu… / He put steel through his own hand to make me listen. / I have met one other man with eyes like that.
euija: Oh?
gesomun: You. / I do not yet know which of you frightens me more.
euija: Flattery. Keep going.
gesomun: It was not flattery.
gesomun: You came with three. You’re leaving with five. / …Did Your Majesty come as an envoy, or to do some shopping?
euija: I have a gift for gathering people. You have a gift for reducing them.
courtmaid: Your Majesty. Goryeo is cold. / Shall we… warm you?
courtmaid: With mouths. With thighs. / Even while you look at the map.
euija: I am aware. / …Both of you, come. / Quietly. / Before Commander Yeon… hears.
courtmaid: So tonight two of us will come in.
courtmaid: One body isn’t enough… to hold Your Majesty. / From both sides… at once.
euija: …Don’t flatter.
euija: The body… is already answering.
courtmaid: It isn’t flattery.
courtmaid: The hands… remember. / Where Your Majesty… told them to go last night.
In the morning he rides south with all five. Nobody raises the subject of the extra two. He carries a map of Danghangseong in his head, and Yeon’s warning about Chunchu folded away like a knife he intends to use later.
Why does the Eternal General flinch at one Silla name? Go back to a ditch, a white horse, and an unknown captain…!

=== EPISODE 27: Nangbi (629) [flashback]
Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo wall. The men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Nangbi Fortress, 629)] In the eighth month of autumn, in the forty-sixth year of Geonbok, a gichuk year, the king sent the Ichan Im Malli, the Pajinchan Yongchun and Baekryong, and the Sopan Daein and Seohyeon at the head of an army to attack the Goguryeo fortress of Nangbi. The Goguryeo men came out and struck back without warning. Our side was beaten and many died; the men’s spirit was broken, and they had no heart left to fight.
He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.
yushin: Father. We’re losing. / They say you shake a coat by the collar to make it hang straight, and lift the head-rope to open a net. / …Let me be the collar.
seohyeon: …Put your helmet on. / Then go.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Nangbi Fortress, 629)] Yushin was then captain of the Middle Banner. He went before his father, took off his helmet, and said: “Our army is beaten. All my life I have held myself to loyalty to the country and duty to my parents; facing battle, I cannot fail to be brave.”
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Nangbi Fortress, 629)] “I have heard that when you shake the collar the coat hangs straight, and when you lift the head-rope the net opens. Let me be that rope and that collar.” Then he mounted his horse, drew his sword, leapt the trench, and went in and out of the enemy lines; he cut down their general and came back carrying his head.
The white horse takes the trench in one jump that the men in it will describe for the rest of their lives, usually with their hands. In, out. In again. The third time Yushin comes back there is something heavy hanging from his saddle, and the men in the trench are already climbing out.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinpyeong, year 51 (629)] Then he mounted, drew his sword and rode straight at the enemy line. Three times he went in and three times he came out, and each time he went in he either cut down a commander or tore down a banner.
He brings the weight on his saddle back to the command post and sets it down in the mud in front of his father, wrapped in a torn banner, because he does not know what else a son is supposed to do with a general’s head. The staff officers wait for the speech. Seohyeon looks at the bundle, then at the boy, for long enough that someone coughs.
seohyeon: …Your helmet’s crooked.
He reaches up and straightens it himself, both hands, the way you fix a boy’s collar before a feast, and then turns away and shouts for his officers before anyone can see his face. It is the most Kim Seohyeon has ever said to his son about anything, and Yushin will carry it longer than the helmet.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Nangbi Fortress, 629)] Our soldiers saw it, rode the turn of the battle and threw themselves into the attack. They took more than five thousand heads and a thousand prisoners alive. The people inside the walls were so terrified that none dared resist, and all came out and surrendered.
That night he asks the groom what the white horse is called. The groom says it has no name; it came from the royal stable as a spare. Yushin looks at it for a long time, at the mud on its chest and the way it still will not quite stand still.
yushin: Hangyul. / …It means steady. It came back steady. All three times.
The few who get out of Nangbi walk north for nine days with the story, and it grows a little at every well. By Pyongyang the white horse has cleared the trench at a gallop with a general’s head in one hand and a banner in the other, and the man on it has a name the Goguryeo clerks must write down for the first time.
[QUOTE Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 20, Goguryeo Annals — King Yeongnyu, year 12 (629)] Twelfth year, autumn, the eighth month: the Silla general Kim Yushin invaded the eastern border and broke Nangbi Fortress.
In Pyongyang the report is read to the king twice, the second time because he asks for it. At the back of the hall the Yeon heir, twenty-four, stands with his arms folded, the way he stands everywhere.
yeongnyu: Kim Yushin… a banner captain. / We have never heard the name.
gesomun: You’ll hear it again. / One man jumps one ditch and five thousand of ours lie down. That’s a captain? That’s a sword. / Silla’s sword.
## The High Commander’s House
Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Taejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around.
Tonight he does not take off his boots. He sits at the low table with a copy of the Nangbi report, the one the king asked to hear twice, and reads it a third time with his finger under the lines.
gesomun: Father. You’re still on that? / It’s one fortress. We take it back by spring.
yeontaejo: Sit. / …Five thousand heads. Off one charge. How many men have you seen do that?
gesomun: One. / You. At the Colossal River.
yeontaejo: I had thirty thousand men and a river on my side. / He had a ditch and a horse.
Gesomun has seen his father angry, drunk and bleeding, and once, when he was seven, riding home from the Colossal River with a Sui banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. He has never seen him frightened of a piece of paper. He finds he does not know where to put his hands.
yeontaejo: Thirty-four, and still a banner captain. Silla won’t let a Gaya grandson climb any faster. / They’re wasting him. They won’t waste him forever.
gesomun: Then I’ll kill him before they stop.
yeontaejo: You’ll try. / Listen to me. Never on a field he picked. Never when you’re angry. And when this city tells you he’s only a captain, don’t believe it.
gesomun: His Majesty already did.
yeontaejo: His Majesty heard it twice and asked the Summit what to do. / Do you know what the Summit did? Argued half a day over who pays to rebuild the fort. Nobody said his name. Not once. / Ten years I’ve sat in that room. They’ll lose this country one granary at a time and call it caution.
Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once.
gesomun: …Kim Yushin.
That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark. Thirteen years later, Gesomun will hear that sword is riding for the prince in his prison. He’ll remember a hall, a report read twice, and his father reading it a third time.
Thirteen years on, the banner captain has a queen, a title, and a long list of Baekje fortresses. He's working through it…!

=== EPISODE 28: Forty Fortresses (642)
In the meantime Queen Sunduk sends her general, Kim Yushin, against Baekje.
euija: I-i-it’s Kim Yushin!!
euija: You’ve never heard of Kim Yushin…?
euija: You fool — Kim Yushin is the Greatest Blade of Samhan…! / Yeon Gesomun, General Gyebek — tell them all to stand aside. Or tell Gyebek the title is still disputed. He will not laugh.
Over the next few years Yushin takes more than forty fortresses.
In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. At home they toast it. Both sides add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet. Until he does, “greatest blade” is a tavern argument with two right answers.
yushin: After the twentieth, nobody was counting.
chunchu: And you kept taking them anyway.
yushin: …If I stopped, they would invent a reason for my stopping.
Between campaigns he still goes alone to the cavern lake. The stone in the story is his father’s. His own pocket is empty. He undresses anyway.
narim: You came with a question, or you came because the hill opened. / Either is fine. Sit down before you fall in again. And take the rest off. I want the question from a bare man.
yushin: Three things. / The northern door. The queen’s count. How long I may stay.
golhwa: Stay is not a number, marshal. / Sit. Unnie will do the other two. I’ll do the one she pretends isn’t counsel.
golhwa: It involves my mouth.
Hyullé does not speak. She has already warmed the far ledge. Her eyes are on his mouth while Narim answers the north. He will ride before I finish a sentence.
narim: Yeon’s door is a guest-door only from one side. / The queen’s count is the one they will not let her finish. Bring her the west in numbers. Do not stand in front of the chair. / Take what you need. Leave before Golhwa asks you to stay. She will ask.
narim: She will also try to sit on you. I’m only warning you about one of those.
golhwa: Stay. In the water.
golhwa: On me, if you can bear the youngest being first.
yushin: Guest-door. Numbers. Behind the chair. Leave before stay. / I have the three answers. That is enough.
euija: Yushin, my friend~~ / My men stop eating at the sound of your name.
One star over Samhan tonight. Three men are looking up at it, and every one of them wants to be the King for All…!

=== EPISODE 29: The Eastern Star (642)
yushin: Well — is it enough now? / We have given Baekje a proper beating…
yushin: So then… do you mean to drag the King of Baekje back too?
chunchu: Brother… the grudge is mine. I know that. / But something else is moving, and it is not me moving it.
chunchu: Brother… I had little interest in any of it. / A wife I loved, a peaceful household. / I believed that much would be enough. / But the world—
yushin: Chunchu, what on earth are you saying…
chunchu: The eastern star shines especially bright tonight… / Brother… let us go and take it now. / That old palace of ours… / the dream we had when we were young… / The “King for All”, I mean…!
yushin: …I told you. That one is a planet.
chunchu: Thirty years and you are still saying that.
euija: Gyebek. You grew up inside that palace. / You have watched men go mad reaching for a chair. / A man is one of two things — a king, or a slave. / There are slaves in crowns and kings begging at the west gate. / One request.
gyebek: I will obey.
euija: No. Do not follow me. / One day I will give you a stupid order. More than one. / Judge it yourself. / I wear the crown. You are still the king of your own life…!
gyebek: Your Majesty… why are you telling me this?
euija: Gyebek… a man should hold a larger dream. / The “King for All”, I mean…!
gyebek: Your Majesty. / I saw Gesomun again.
He touches the left side of his neck when he says it, where the old burn scar runs down under his collar.
The banquet hall has been scrubbed for three nights. Yeon climbs to a cave in the hill above the river. Nobody prays there lightly. The marches say the stone still remembers bowstrings.
He kneels at the mouth and lays a crow-stamped ring-pommel on the stone. He does not ask forgiveness for the hall. He asks for witnesses.
gesomun: The Holy King forged a country here. / I too… will forge one with my own hands.
gesomun: …All my life I did not know what I was for. / Most men are born, and live a while, and die. / You gave me monsters. / Thank you for giving me a direction.
gesomun: Until every bone in me is broken. / Until every jewel in my heart is cracked through. / I will not let go of this. / The “King for All”, I mean…!
Gesomun wants a country. Far to the west, the man who owns half the world is trying to pronounce his name…!
